lesson_title: Why Tokyo Is Already Having Supper
hook_text: Three in the afternoon in Johannesburg. In Tokyo, supper is already on the table. One number explains it.
clip_script: The Earth spins all the way round, three hundred and sixty degrees, every twenty-four hours. Divide it: fifteen degrees every hour. That is the number. Every fifteen degrees east, the clock is one hour later, because places further east spin into the sunlight first. Durban sees the sun at its highest almost an hour before Cape Town does. The world agreed on time zones, stripes about fifteen degrees wide starting at Greenwich. South Africa uses one stripe, two hours ahead of Greenwich. Tokyo is seven hours ahead of us, so three in the afternoon here is ten at night there. And out in the Pacific there is a line where the date itself jumps. Samoa once hopped across it and skipped an entire Friday. Fifteen degrees, one hour. East is ahead.
visual_style: A whiteboard globe spinning under a torch beam, fifteen-degree stripes lighting up one by one with clocks above them; a calendar page for Friday tearing away over the Pacific.
pacing: Quick derivation of fifteen, a smooth sweep of time zones, a playful final beat with the skipped Friday.
